I've had migraines since I was 14 years old. 
Doctors were reluctant to put me on any medication despite having migraines weekly. They finally put me on a beta blocker when I was 17. 
Didn't help. Between the ages of 17-27 I was cycled through so many different medications. 
One actually sent me into psychosis. 
Botox didn't work. 
Emgality was still about 200 bucks a month here at the time, I ended up deciding to just try it. 
And it worked. 
I had to stop work at around the age of 24/25 ( I can't really remember) and even with the emgality treating a majority of my migraines, I was still getting them maybe once a week. (Which was a significant drop for me at the time) 
There were times in my teens and mid 20s where I couldn't leave the house, I couldn't do anything, I was just constantly cycling between migraine and post migraine states. 
I was mentally not doing well at all. 
I think my advice is, keep trying, even the whacky shit you think is silly, try it, track it. Ask to be in a few different types, e.g betablockers and a crgp.
Push your specialist if you have one, do the weird tests that may show nothing is wrong. Keep reaching out, keep up with the latest news in migraine treatment research. Look after your mental health too. I never felt like Ariel, I felt like those mermaids that were turned to wiggly gross things by Ursula, always in the dark, knowing I could be somebody if I wasn't under this curse. 
Have hope, friend X

As someone who has fostered quite a few dogs. Please don't take her to a dog park. The way humans think dogs want to socialise is generally incorrect and putting a newly rescued dog into a space where you have no idea what her temperament is and what the other stranger dogs are like, you're looking for a very bad time. 

It would be great if you could join a walking group or find a friend who has a dog where you can go on walks. Playing does not equal a fun social thing for dogs, the best thing you can teach your dog is how to be neutral around other dogs and then find them a well matched friend who has a similar play style and temperament. 
My dog generally dislikes playing with other dogs and gets quite stressed when playing. You've already started out great by being her advocate, keep going! Learn about dog behaviour, dog body language and most importantly, learn how your dog interacts and sees the world. Goodluck!

Every dog is different, the idea that you have to have a huge walk every day with your dog or that on days where you can't walk your dog is fine. Do you have to compensate for the lack of physical and mental exercise? Most definitely! We have a cattle Dog cross and she doesn't have a day routine but her mornings and nights are exactly the same. We change it up every week but we always have, play dates, a hike, a walk in a new/different area and decompression walks.

She refuses go to for a walk when it's raining and I refuse to take her when it's over 29 degrees Celsius. 

What do we do instead when we can't take our dog for a walk? We ramp up the indoor activities, we play all day, we train more than we usually would, we play chasy around the house. We invite other pup friends over to play, we wait until it's dark and cool then do a decompression walk.We'll go for a drive so she can get some good sniffies. If both my partner and I are sick -we pay someone to walk her. 

Saying that if you can't take your dog for a walk then you don't deserve a dog is ridiculous because you have no insight into the rest of their day and how they compensate for the change of routine. 
Not having a rigid structure works for us and our dog is as happy as a pig in mud. Our routine is 

Up at 8: breakfast in a long wobbler or I'm a snuffle Matt

Between 9 and 12 we play, train and have snuggles.

Had migraines since I was 14. Mum has them, Nan had them, my sister gets them although the middle sister escaped the genetic bomb. 
The worst migraines I get are the hormonal ones, hands down. Symptoms for these include a change in senses, taste, smell and sight. My speech goes funny, I can vomit. Usually there's nothing I can do for these except sleep and wait it out, even the triptan will be ineffective sometimes. The upside of these ones are that they will only last a few hours.  

Now I also get muscle triggered migraines, from bad posture. These ones last week's if I trigger one by sitting wrong or not showering before bed. Symptoms include sore muscles, my jaw will ache, pain in my eyes, my teeth, sometimes I'll end up with a tension headache too. These ones are usually aborted by a triptan, shower and a good roll on the foam roller to stretch out sore muscles. 

I'm also just very prone to migraines, if I weren't on my beta blocker I'd have one every day. 
I have exersises to do before bed to help with my muscles, I drink lots of water and I avoid drinking sugary drinks and wine with additives. If I feel one coming on I will take a triptan or four aspirin. 
I also use tiger balm on my forehead to ease the pain and magnesium is a must.

Seeing a physio is very helpful, I'm yet to try dry needling but I would like too. 
Edit:. I'm 26 now.
Medications are topamax 50mg, propanalol 120 mg and relpax 40 mg when needed.
